body: IT services firms sell people-hours and managed outcomes to global enterprises, with ~55–60% of revenue from the US. They make money on a labour arbitrage: offshore billing rates against Indian salaries, plus pyramid management. Key metrics: constant-currency revenue growth, deal TCV and book-to-bill, attrition, utilisation, EBIT margin, headcount additions, revenue per employee, top-client concentration and vertical mix (BFSI, retail, manufacturing). Cycle drivers: US/EU IT budgets and discretionary spend, BFSI health, the USD/INR rate (a weaker rupee adds ~30–40 bps of margin per 1% depreciation), technology shifts (cloud in 2020–22; GenAI deflating application services in 2025–26) and H-1B and visa policy. Lead indicators: Accenture quarterly bookings, Gartner IT spending forecasts, US non-farm IT employment, Naukri JobSpeak, hyperscaler capex, deal announcements. Winners rode each new wave early (TCS and Infosys with Y2K and offshoring; Persistent and Coforge with digital in 2020–24), kept strong client mining and protected margins. Losers clung to a legacy mix (Wipro's 2015–23 stagnation, Mphasis's HP-channel decline) or made acquisition-led pivots that diluted margins. Valuation: P/E roughly 15–20x in 2013–19 and ~30–35x at the Dec 2021 peak. Nifty IT was ~18x in Jun 2026 against a 27x 7-year median. Nov 2026: Infosys grew only +1.5% CC YoY in Q2 FY27 and cut FY27 guidance to 1–2%, even though large-deal TCV was $5.2 bn and AI revenue grew 29% QoQ. Traps: TCV that does not convert, and rupee-led growth.

data.business_model: Time-and-materials + fixed-price/managed services; arbitrage of offshore cost vs onshore billing.
data.current_state_nov_2026: Infosys Q2 FY27: $5.145 bn, +1.5% YoY CC (+1.2% QoQ), FY27 guidance cut to 1–2% (from 1.5–3%), op margin 21.0%, large-deal TCV $5.2 bn (62% net new), AI revenue +29% QoQ. TCS Q2 preview ~0.5–0.6% QoQ CC. Rupee growth (+10.7%) flatters reported numbers.
data.cycle_drivers: US GDP/BFSI spend, tech-shift cycles, USD/INR, wage inflation and supply, visa policy, GenAI productivity pass-through to clients.
lead_indicators: US BLS computer systems design employment
traps: Mega-deal TCV that is mostly renewals or back-ended
Cheap vs history when terminal growth has structurally fallen (GenAI deflation)
Margin 'beats' from lower subcontracting/hiring freezes that precede growth problems
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Global enterprise IT budget -> hyperscalers/SaaS vendors capture platform value -> SIs (Accenture) -> Indian IT (implementation, run, BPO) -> mid-tier/ER&D specialists. Highest margins in proprietary platforms/products and niche ER&D; lowest in commoditised app maintenance (most exposed to GenAI deflation).
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: early in each wave, high client mining (count of $100m clients rising), focused verticals, low attrition, disciplined pricing. Losers: legacy infra/app maintenance mix, management churn, expensive acquisitions to buy growth.

title: Sector playbook: Indian IT services
